findings.text: follow-on: the recorded after_suite names revision 7d5dad01934ecc8599b121e3b9f527e1b1d6a2d2 and the two-file command `pytest ... tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py tests/test_one_of_two_racing_reviews_survives.py`, but no log on disk was produced at that revision or with that command; its own log_path (gate-guard-wrapped.log) is headed rev 4dc8ff94 and runs only tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py, and at 4dc8ff94 the guard case's wrapped() instrument does not accept own_run_id, so the case cannot pass there — the log was measured from a tree carrying the not-yet-committed wrapper fix, and its revision header understates the tree it measured.

follow-on: `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` compares `(claim.registered_at, claim.run_id) > (own_registered_at, own_run_id)` over raw strings, with registered_at read as `str(pointer.get("created_at") or "")`, whereas the codebase orders timestamps through `parse_utc` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:4669, :4842). Lexicographic order equals chronology only for a single uniform spelling; a live pointer whose created_at carries an offset instead of a trailing Z, or sub-second precision, sorts wrongly, and the run-id tie-break by run id settles only equal stamps — a wall-clock skew between the two dispatchers ranks the later registration as the earlier one.

follow-on: the rule is first-wins with no fallback, so if the registered-first dispatch withdraws later for an unrelated reason (a budget hold, a backend ceiling, a crash) after the later dispatch has already refused on ordering, the paths are left with no worker — the state this node removes is only removed while the winner then survives its own launch.

follow-on: the third production call site of `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` — the `_raise_live_scope_conflict` facade — passes neither own_run_id nor own_registered_at and builds its claims with the default empty registered_at and launched=False, so the ordering never applies there and a race reaching this seam still withdraws the pair; nothing in reckon/ or tests/ calls the facade today, so the exposure is a caller outside this tree.

follow-on: commit 7d5dad01 changes this file, outside the reviewed node's declared write fence (dispatch.py, the new test file, the evidence fragment); the edit restores a test the change broke, is coordinator-directed, and is declared with its reason in the manifest's follow_ons, so it is a disclosed deviation — but the fence alone does not name it, and the reviewed run's changed_paths lists a path its orientation_write_paths does not.

item_verdicts.diff: read against base 2a0696ba; dispatch.py gains `registered_at`/`launched` on `_RepositoryScopeClaim` (read from the live pointer's created_at and worktree-or-pid), a threaded `registered_at` on `_publish_launch_claim`, the ordering helper, and `own_run_id`/`own_registered_at` threaded into both `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` calls; commit 7d5dad01 adds the two keyword-only parameters to the guard test's wrapped() instrument only. No other production line changes.
item_verdicts.done_when: tests/test_one_of_two_racing_reviews_survives.py drives the rule against its worst inputs: :212 plants a peer claim registered after this dispatch and asserts the earlier dispatch keeps the single live pointer while the peer survives to refuse itself; :245 plants one registered before and asserts this dispatch refuses naming the earlier run and leaves nothing of itself behind; :272 asserts a launched peer refuses whatever the order; :322 asserts the ordering itself — equal times fall to the run id, a launched claim refuses, an unorderable claim refuses, and a dispatch holding no claim refuses. Each case plants the peer claim from inside the worktree seam, so it is read exactly as a peer dispatch's own claim would be read.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that exactly one of two dispatches racing for the same write paths survives, the other refusing and naming the winner; at head 7d5dad01 `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1847) disregards a peer claim that carries no worktree and no pid (`launched=False`) and whose (registered_at, run_id) sorts strictly after this dispatch's own, reached inside `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` (dispatch.py:1919) from both dispatch admission checks (dispatch.py:4873 and dispatch.py:5352) with this dispatch's own run id and registration timestamp. The rule is antisymmetric — the earlier registrant disregards every later one and the later ones fall through to the pre-existing refusal — so exactly one proceeds, and the three terminal cases (a launched peer, an empty registration, a dispatch holding no claim) all refuse as before, which is the goal.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the reviewed manifest; status complete, commits 7d5dad01934ecc8599b121e3b9f527e1b1d6a2d2 and 4dc8ff94b3ac70d6f198e84e4262cd3a6b9e40c7 over base 2a0696ba544bdeb8fd66e0c2bdbf483488fa3e6d, base-existing-conflicts.log (2 failed/3 passed) as the baseline arm and gate-guard-wrapped.log as the after arm, negative_control_log recorded and red at 2 failed/2 passed EXIT=1; added_failure_count 0 with no ids across the two arms; two pre-existing failures in tests/test_dispatch_launch_is_not_its_own_conflict.py recorded as outside the node's scope.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest's orientation names reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_one_of_two_racing_reviews_survives.py and the evidence fragment; commit 4dc8ff94 changes exactly those three (dispatch.py +66/-1, test file +363, fragment +29) and commit 7d5dad01 changes tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py alone (+4) — a path outside that fence, declared with its reason in the manifest's follow_ons and directed by the coordinator's resume advice.

justifications.durability: the guards are real and independent — my own order-blind mutation reddens the race case and the ordering case — and the tests assert the ordering against its worst inputs, but two gaps survive: the ordering compares the registration stamp as a raw string where the codebase orders timestamps through parse_utc, so a differently-spelled or host-skewed stamp can invert the order; and the rule is first-wins with no fallback, so a registered-first dispatch that withdraws later for an unrelated reason leaves the paths with no worker.
justifications.evidence: I re-ran the node's own after arm independently at the reviewed head — `PYTHONPATH=<worktree> pytest -q tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py tests/test_one_of_two_racing_reviews_survives.py` -> 18 passed, EXIT=0 (reviewer-head-arm.log) — and reproduced the negative control myself, mutating `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` to the order-blind constant and observing 2 failed/2 passed, EXIT=1 (reviewer-negative-control.log), matching the run's own red log; the added-failure count derived from the manifest's own baseline_suite/after_suite logs is 0 with no ids. Weakness: the recorded after_suite names revision 7d5dad01 and a two-file command that no log on disk records, and its baseline arm runs a narrower file set than the head arm (see the finding at the manifest).
justifications.fit: the new symbols are mechanism-named (`_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival`, `registered_at`, `launched`, `claim_registered_at`), the comments state why a still-composing claim is outranked and an unorderable one is refused, the test docstring states the race and the rule rather than a changelog, and no plan, phase, ticket or version label appears in the change.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every clause of the goal is present and correct in the diff, and I reconstructed the antisymmetry by hand: `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` returns True only for a peer that carries no worktree-or-pid and registered after this dispatch's own, so of two racers exactly one disregards the other and passes its first admission check; the still-composing shape it keys on is exactly the launch claim published before the worktree is cut (the first check at dispatch.py:4873 runs before _create_worktree at dispatch.py:5003), and the second check at dispatch.py:5352 re-reads live claims excluding this run by identity.
justifications.scope_discipline: commit 4dc8ff94 is exactly the three declared paths and the reviewed worktree is clean at head; commit 7d5dad01 is one file outside the fence, restored to accept the two keywords the change threads (tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py), declared with its reason in the manifest and directed by the coordinator's resume advice, so it is a disclosed scope extension rather than an undeclared one.
